article.Citation/Title: Pagni, B. A., Zeifman, R. J., Mennenga, S. E., Carrithers, B. M., Goldway, N., Bhatt, S., O'Donnell, K. C., Ross, S., & Bogenschutz, M. P. (2025). Multidimensional personality changes following psilocybin-assisted therapy in patients with alcohol use disorder: Results from a double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial. American Journal of Psychiatry.
article.InterventionDescription: Psilocybin (25 mg, then 30-40 mg/kg as printed) vs. active placebo diphenhydramine; two medication sessions 4 weeks apart; 12 weeks manualized PSI psychotherapy; NYU/UNM sites.

article.Citation/Title: This is a secondary analysis of personality-trait data collected within the double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of psilocybin-assisted therapy for AUD whose primary drinking outcomes were reported in the parent trial: Bogenschutz MP, Ross S, Bhatt S, et al. 'Percentage of heavy drinking days following psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy vs placebo in the treatment of adult patients with alcohol use disorder: a randomized clinical trial.' JAMA Psychiatry 2022;79:953-962 (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02061293), cited as ref. 18 throughout this article.
article.EligibleYN: Criterion (a): eligible as a secondary analysis of trial data per the boundary case rule -- the parent RCT (Bogenschutz et al. 2022) randomized 95 adults with AUD to psilocybin vs. active placebo with a prospectively planned intervention; this paper reuses that trial's design and prospectively collected personality/drinking measures. Criterion (b): satisfied because substance-use outcomes (drinks-per-day change/posttreatment DpD via TLFB, WHO drinking-risk categories) are reported throughout Results, even though they are secondary to this article's own stated primary personality outcome.
article.Outcome: This article's stated primary outcome is personality-trait change (five preplanned between-group ANCOVAs on NEO-PI-R factors: neuroticism, extraversion, openness, agreeableness, conscientiousness), NOT a drinking outcome -- flagged per instructions as a discrepancy from the AUD-review's usual SUD-outcome focus. Among the four traits explicitly hypothesized a priori (neuroticism, extraversion, openness, conscientiousness), reported between-group partial eta-squared values are numerically tied at 0.07 for extraversion/openness/conscientiousness vs. 0.06 for neuroticism (Table 1, 'Effect of Treatment' columns), so no single trait is unambiguously 'largest.' I selected neuroticism as the representative co-equal primary because it is listed first in both the Abstract's Results sentence and the Introduction's hypothesis ordering, and because it is the trait mechanistically tied to this article's central AUD-specific hypothesis (the neuroticism facet impulsiveness is separately correlated with drinking outcomes) -- unlike openness, whose increase paradoxically moved further from normative levels and is not cleanly 'favorable.' This is a judgment call; extraversion or openness (both eta_p=0.07) would be equally defensible alternate picks and are recorded here for transparency. Value taken from Table 1, first data row (Neuroticism), 'Effect of Treatment' block.
article.SD: Table 1 prints the between-group ANCOVA treatment-effect statistic for neuroticism as 'F (df=1,18) = 5.20.' This df is internally inconsistent with the ANCOVA covariate-term df reported elsewhere in the Results text for the same model family ('F=2.29, df=1, 81, p=0.13' for the openness covariate), which implies an error df near 81 (consistent with N=84). The printed '18' may be a transposition/OCR artifact of '81,' but per protocol I report the value exactly as printed rather than constructing a decoding theory. Downstream users should verify the correct df before relying on this statistic.
article.PVal: Uncorrected p=0.03 for the neuroticism between-group treatment effect, paired with F(1,18)=5.20 in the same Table 1 row. The FDR-corrected value is pFDR=0.05 (also printed in the same row); both survive the study's own significance threshold, but the uncorrected value is reported per the field rule to pair exactly with the SD statistic.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: N=84 (psilocybin N=44, placebo N=40) is the full analyzed sample for all reported ANCOVA/t-test results, per Methods: 'Of the original 95 participants who were randomized to treatment, two were not treated with study medication and nine did not complete pre- and posttreatment NEO questionnaires. Thus, 84 participants... were included in the analyses.'

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: Setting (NYU/UNM sites), intervention, comparator, outcomes, randomization, blinding, statistics, results, and funding/COI are all clearly described in this article. Eligibility criteria are only gestured at (comorbid psychiatric conditions and other SUDs were excluded, per Limitations) with full inclusion/exclusion detail deferred to companion papers (refs 18, 27, 28), so coded N. Harms/AEs are not assessed or described anywhere in this article's own text (it is a personality-focused secondary analysis with no safety section), so coded N. Sample_size_power coded Y on the bare 'it was a pilot study, and larger clinical trials are needed to confirm clinical significance' statement in Limitations, per the rule that a bare underpowered statement counts as discussed -- a close call, noted here.

article.Power: Coded 1 based solely on the Limitations statement 'it was a pilot study, and larger clinical trials are needed to confirm clinical significance,' treated as a bare acknowledgment of limited power per the coding rule. No explicit a priori or post hoc power calculation is given anywhere in this article's text; this is a close call.
article.Retention (%): Denominator is the randomized N (95, all randomized at once with no separate enrolled-but-not-randomized figure). Completers = 84 (final analytic sample). 84/95 x 100 = 88.42%, rounded to 88.4.
article.InclusionExclusionCriteria: Coded 0: this article states only that 'the present study excluded many patients with comorbid psychiatric conditions and other substance use disorders' (Discussion) without restating a full inclusion/exclusion list; the complete criteria are deferred to companion design papers (refs 18, 27, 28), so they are not clearly stated within this article itself.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: Coded 0: income was reported (mean annual income psilocybin $266.7K, placebo $147.7K; Limitations note mean incomes >$140,000), but it describes an affluent, homogeneous sample rather than explicit inclusion or description of low-SES participants (no low-income eligibility or public-insurance enrollment mentioned). Judgment call given the field's illustrative examples skew toward low-SES inclusion.
article.BaseStatus: Coded 'Severe' based on Results: mean 31.56 years (SD=11.47) alcohol dependent, mean 5.25 of 7 DSM-IV dependence criteria met, mean SIP total score 20.42 (SD=9.03), and mean 52.57% (SD=30.32) heavy drinking days in the past month -- a long-duration, high-criteria-count AUD sample.
article.Age_Median: Not reported as a numeric value anywhere in the main article text; baseline age is referenced only as a variable examined for group differences ('Baseline treatment group differences were examined with respect to... age...'), with actual figures deferred to online supplemental Table S1, which was not provided in the converted text.
article.PercentFem: Not reported as a percentage in the main article text; sex/gender is referenced only as a baseline-comparison variable, with figures deferred to online supplemental Table S1, not present in the converted text.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Article states participants were 'predominantly white (~77%)' (the semicolon before 77% in the converted text appears to be a rendering artifact of a tilde/approx symbol, not a numeric error). Non-white percent computed as 100 - 77 = 23.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 0: Limitations explicitly describe the sample as 'relatively small, homogeneous... (i.e., mean annual incomes >$140,000, and 77% white)' and speculate this may reflect 'recruiting from highly urban geographical areas' -- indicating a highly selected, non-representative volunteer sample rather than a real-world clinical/community population.
article.InterventionDescription: The article prints the psilocybin dose as '25 mg and 30-40 mg/kg,' which is almost certainly a garbled/erroneous figure (30-40 mg/kg total-body-weight psilocybin dosing would be far outside any plausible clinical range; standard PAT dosing is typically expressed as mg/70kg or a fixed mg/kg on the order of 0.3-0.4 mg/kg). Reported exactly as printed per protocol rather than silently corrected; flagged here as an internally implausible number.
article.HarmsAssessed: Coded 0 to agree with SafetyReported='N': this article's own text contains no Adverse Events/Safety section, table, or explicit statement about AE assessment. Harms were certainly assessed in the parent trial (Bogenschutz et al. 2022, ref 18), but that assessment is not reported or described within this secondary personality-analysis article.
article.Double+Blind: Coded 1 for the nominal double-blind, active-placebo design, but flagging a functional-blinding limitation the authors themselves report: 'approximately 94% of participants in the parent trial accurately guessed their treatment assignment,' raising concern about functional unblinding despite the double-blind protocol.
article.MentalHealthChangeMeasured: Coded 0: no validated clinical mental-health instrument (e.g., depression/anxiety scale) was administered in this article; the NEO-PI-R 'depression' item is a personality facet, not a clinical mental-health outcome measure. Judgment call given the facet's name overlaps with a mental-health construct.
article.CessationMeasured: Coded 0: the drinking outcome used (drinks-per-day, TLFB) and WHO risk categories track quantity/frequency and risk level, not a distinct binary cessation/abstinence outcome.
article.RelapseMeasured: Coded 0: drinking is tracked longitudinally (weeks 0-36) but is not framed by the authors as a 'relapse' or 'return to use' outcome distinct from ongoing consumption level.
article.Followup in months: The trial comprises 12 weeks of treatment (medication sessions + psychotherapy, weeks 0-12) followed by an explicitly stated 'additional 24 weeks' of follow-up (Abstract Methods), reaching the week-36 personality assessment. Measuring from end of treatment (week 12) per the field rule: 24 weeks / ~4.33 weeks per month = 5.5 months. Note the article itself repeatedly frames week 36 differently, as '7 months after the second medication session' / '7-8 months posttreatment' (measured from the second dosing session or from baseline, respectively, both ~8 months) -- these framings differ materially from the end-of-treatment figure used here.
article.Pos Result Y/N: Coded 1: the primary personality-trait analysis (neuroticism, extraversion, openness) showed significant treatment effects favoring psilocybin, all surviving FDR correction. Secondary correlational analyses also linked reduced impulsiveness to lower posttreatment drinking, reinforcing a positive overall result, though this article's own primary outcome is personality change rather than drinking.
article.SafetyReported: Coded 'N': this article contains no Adverse Events, Safety, or Side-effects section, table, or explicit statement assessing harms. It is a secondary personality-outcomes analysis; the single general remark that 'close clinical supervision... is necessary for ensuring safety' (Discussion) is a general observation, not a report of an actual safety assessment conducted in this study.
article.AnyAEReported: Coded 'NA' because SafetyReported='N' -- the article is silent on AEs/safety entirely, per the three-state coding table.
article.NumDistinctAEs: Coded 'NA' because SafetyReported='N'; no AE data of any kind appear in this article's text.
article.NParticipantsWithAE: Coded 'NA' because SafetyReported='N'; no AE participant counts appear in this article's text.
article.AE_denominator: Coded '.' (never 'NA' per field rule) because no safety assessment was reported in this article, so no AE-assessed population denominator exists to report.
article.ArmScope: Coded 'NA': with no AE data reported at all in this article, arm scope for AE reporting genuinely does not apply.
article.WorstSeverity: Coded 'NA' because SafetyReported='N', per the three-state coding table.

config_proposal.note: Outcome is the between-group partial eta-squared (eta_p^2=0.06) for the ANCOVA treatment effect on neuroticism (Table 1), selected as the representative co-equal primary among four a priori-hypothesized personality traits (see rationale.article.Outcome for the tie and the judgment call). Proposing method='eta_p' per instruction. Confidence is 'approx' rather than 'clean' because: (a) this Tier-1 effect size is a personality outcome, not the substance-use outcome this AUD review otherwise targets, so its inclusion on a SUD-focused forest plot is itself an interpretive assumption; and (b) the paired F-statistic's printed df (1,18) is inconsistent with the df=1,81 implied elsewhere in the same ANCOVA model family, so conversion precision cannot be fully verified from the article as printed.
